newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's teachers skip classes for strike.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's teachers skip classes for strike.

text.p: Ecuador's teachers walked off the job Wednesday to protest government austerity policies and union leaders said the move opened the way for a general strike.

"Our battle plan starts today with these protests, but we're planning meetings nationwide with members of the (union groupings) Popular Front and United Workers Front to set a date for a joint national strike," National Teachers Union (UNE) President Stalin Vargas told Reuters.
No early turnout was reported for the strike by the 127,000-strong UNE, which could potentially cripple public schools attended by some 2.3 million students.
The strike is the first labor protest faced by the five-month-old administration of President Abdala Bucaram.
Bucaram had recently warned 1997 would be a tough year for the population after the government extended the tax base and scrapped subsidies for gas and public transport.
Local newspapers said the government would also raise electricity and telephone rates by at least 100 percent.
The savings will help finance a fiscal deficit equal to about four percent of GDP and set the framework for a currency convertibility plan.
Minimum monthly wages were frozen at 95,000 sucres ($25.99). Teachers with 10 years seniority earn 463,000 sucres (126.6 dollars).
